summary:
**Conversation Overview**

The person asked Claude to locate all their skills stored in the system and package them into a downloadable zip file. Claude used bash commands to find all SKILL.md files under `/mnt/skills`, copied the skills directory, and created a zip archive at `/mnt/user-data/outputs/my_skills.zip` (7.3 MB), which was then presented for download.

Claude also provided a detailed inventory of the skills found, organized into three categories: 20 custom user skills (located in `user/`), 7 public skills (located in `public/`), and 23 example skills (located in `examples/`). The custom skills span a range of domains including legal consultation, game design, college advising, agent architecture, video scripting, browser automation, financial data collection, symbolic math, and various prompt optimization tools. Several skill names and descriptions were in Chinese. The public skills included document format handlers (docx, pdf, pptx, xlsx) and design tools, while the example skills covered creative and development utilities.

**Tool Knowledge**

For file system operations in this environment, `find /mnt/skills -name "SKILL.md" | sort` reliably enumerates all skills across subdirectories. The zip workflow that succeeded was: copy the target directory to `/home/claude/` first (`cp -r`), then run `zip -r` from that location targeting `/mnt/user-data/outputs/` as the output destination. Using `present_files` with the exact output path `/mnt/user-data/outputs/my_skills.zip` makes the file available for download.
